item.title: SCP-5827:
item.content:encoded:
This seems like an excuse for a self insert and an excuse for using a drawing in one. There's not really going on with the anomaly or it's origin, holes that other comments mention even in almost non-existent scientific explanation. An intense focus on Nebula's personal life (which also pretty much doesn't exist) is in stark contrast to the cold and calculating nature of the foundation. Honestly I've seen better (imo) skips get discarded and I'd like to see this rewritten at the least.

As a personal aside I've been reading SCP for 6 years and I finally made an account because this broke the "suspension of belief" so hard for me and I wanted to voice that. Sorry, I don't want to discourage the writer and I believe this can be improved so it fits. This is all just my opinion

item.title: SCP-5243:
item.content:encoded:
I actually had a line about that in an older version of the skip! Originally there was a much more complicated calculation of how much containment damage the anomaly did — the first time's calculation was a September's worth of days times a set number, the next time's was an October's worth of days, so on and so forth — and whether or not it honoured leap years was actually going to matter, because there'd be one extra day when February rolled around and that would make a difference between near-total failure and total failure.

I didn't include any of that, because it was TOO FUCKING COMPLICATED lol

But yes, to answer the question you actually asked, the anomaly happens on September 8 no matter how many days there are in February. Because, luckily, it's magic and a teeny tiny bit sentient.

item.title: SCP-5092:
item.content:encoded: If the president doesn't know about the Foundation, I'd have to assume their funding doesn't come from the government (or at least, not in any part the US government). item.title: Canst thou draw out Leviathan with an Amortization? or his Tongue with a Bribe which thou lettest down?:
SCP-5104:
item.content:encoded:
Shouldn't the several hundred additional entities receive SCP designations? Shouldn't the Foundation perhaps take an interest in establishing communication with this species, if only in order to negotiate a less Veil-endangering place for them to portal in next time?

The Foundation presented in this scip seems amateurish and sloppy. Even compliant sentient entities are nontrivial to contain. It doesn't help that we're just offhandedly told that the second round of containment was successful, easy peasy, as if the evaluator is carefree and disinterested. There isn't even a cliché note about administering amnestics to witnesses.

I guess I'm in the minority, given that the article has 150+ upvotes. It's not all bad. I like the anomaly itself. I think its use of Yelp is cute, in a good way. But even the more cringe-inducing articles of the LOLFoundation era don't present this cavalier an institution.

item.title: SCP-3005:
item.content:encoded:
One of my absolute favorite SCPs. There's just enough there to piece together the narrative, and it's a good narrative. And it easily has one of the best first person descents into madness I've seen in any horror story, and I've seen a lot of those.

Some possibly spoilery thoughts:

+ show block
– hide block

I interpret the light as destroying the metaphysical "anchor" that keeps something squarely in a single reality, making it exist in multiple parallel realities at once, maybe even every possible reality at once. That's why the researcher says they're not ready for "what's out there"; every possible reality in the Foundation's carefully monitored test chambers is much easier to deal with than the chaos of the world outside. This idea fits in with Star Signals, which describes the Fifth World as your ideal version of reality, the universe sculpted by you into your perfect shape. By severing your connection to one single world, the light gives you the freedom to move to any world. But the human mind isn't made for this, and very strange things happen to a person when they do this.

Most assume the 'body' referred to in "Don't worry about the body" must be a corpse, but I think that line should actually be taken as a much more general statement. As in, don't worry about the physical body, the mind is what matters. Given 3005's general effects on human bodies, this seems like solid advice.

Honestly, I love this SCP, along with 1425, so much that I have trouble accepting any other take on the Fifth Church into my personal headcanon, which I suppose is ironic given the subject material.

item.title: SCP-5866:
item.content:encoded:
I am really teetering on the edge of an upvote for this one. To be clear, I really like the story itself, but…

The one problem I have with this is that I just can't see the Foundation letting any of this happen. I can buy the doctors being sassy as all hell, because, they kinda work in an actual hellscape and humour is a major coping mechanism. The problem I do have is that the Foundation isn't incompetent and is very strict about following the rules (at least in my headcannon). That whole section charter quote, in my headcannon, is not a slap on the wrist kind of violation (did she even get that much?). For me, that would be grounds for immediate and pretty severe disciplinary action.

As I said, I like the story, so it's not even close to a downvote, but this just really messes with how I view the Foundation (and not in a good way). Ah well, I hope this opinion isn't completely outlandish to you. I look forward to seeing more (and hopefully upvoting next time)

item.title: Fault Lines:
